summary: Nintendo and Intelligent Systems' tactical RPG series, including the mainline strategy games, remakes, mobile entries, and Warriors/Tokyo Mirage spinoffs.

entries.title: Fire Emblem: Shadow Dragon and the Blade of Light

emulation.emulator: Nintendo Switch emulator wrapper / Famicom emulator
emulation.notes: Use the official Switch release if owned; otherwise original hardware or legal emulation is the fallback.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Switch release convenience or accurate Famicom emulation

primary.why: For the original 1990 game, the limited Switch release is the most complete official English route and adds modern convenience while preserving the Famicom game; the DS remake is cataloged separately.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Nintendo Switch version if it was purchased before delisting; otherwise use the original Family Computer release or the separate DS remake entry.

entries.remaster_caveats: The DS remake is a separate remake entry, not treated as the same release path for the original Famicom game.

entries.title: Fire Emblem Gaiden

emulation.notes: Accurate Famicom emulation is the practical high-fidelity route for the original.

primary.why: Gaiden's original game exists on Famicom and Japanese Virtual Console; the 3DS Echoes remake is substantial enough to be cataloged separately.
primary.how_to_play: Use original hardware or accurate Famicom emulation for the original game; play Echoes separately for the remake route.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official English release of the original game; Echoes is the separate remake.

entries.title: Fire Emblem: Mystery of the Emblem

emulation.notes: Accurate Super Famicom emulation is the practical high-fidelity route.

primary.why: The Super Famicom original is the baseline version; New Mystery of the Emblem is a separate DS remake entry with changed structure and added content.
primary.how_to_play: Use original Super Famicom hardware or accurate SNES/Super Famicom emulation.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official English release of the original game.

entries.title: Fire Emblem: Genealogy of the Holy War

emulation.notes: Accurate Super Famicom emulation is the practical high-fidelity route.

primary.why: Genealogy remains a Japan-only Super Famicom entry with Virtual Console reissues of the same game; no remake or expanded edition has shipped.
primary.how_to_play: Use original Super Famicom hardware or accurate SNES/Super Famicom emulation; fan-translation use is outside official availability.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official English release has shipped.

entries.title: Fire Emblem: Thracia 776

emulation.notes: Accurate Super Famicom emulation is the practical high-fidelity route.

primary.why: Thracia 776 shipped through Nintendo Power flash cartridge distribution and then a standard ROM cartridge; later Virtual Console releases are reissues of the same Japan-only game.
primary.how_to_play: Use original Super Famicom hardware or accurate SNES/Super Famicom emulation; fan-translation use is outside official availability.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official English release has shipped.

entries.title: Fire Emblem: The Binding Blade

emulation.notes: mGBA or original hardware is the practical high-fidelity route.

primary.why: The Binding Blade remains a Japan-only GBA entry; later Wii U Virtual Console distribution reissues the same game without new story content.
primary.how_to_play: Use original GBA hardware or accurate GBA emulation; fan-translation use is outside official availability.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official English release has shipped.

entries.title: Fire Emblem: Path of Radiance

emulation.notes: Dolphin can raise internal resolution for the highest-fidelity preservation route.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: GameCube emulation at high internal resolution

primary.why: Path of Radiance has no later official port or remaster; the GameCube release is the only content-complete version.
primary.how_to_play: Play on GameCube/Wii backward compatibility or use Dolphin with a legally dumped disc for higher internal resolution.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official remaster or modern port has shipped.

primary.why: Radiant Dawn has no later official port or remaster; the Wii release is the only content-complete version.

entries.title: Fire Emblem: Shadow Dragon

emulation.notes: DS emulation can improve display scaling while preserving the dual-screen layout.

primary.why: Shadow Dragon is the DS remake of the first game and remains its own official version; the DS release is the content baseline, with Virtual Console only reissuing the same game.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Nintendo DS/3DS hardware or a DS emulator with a legally dumped cartridge.

entries.remaster_caveats: No later expanded edition has shipped.

entries.title: Fire Emblem: New Mystery of the Emblem

emulation.notes: DS emulation can improve display scaling while preserving the dual-screen layout.

primary.why: New Mystery is a Japan-only DS remake of Mystery of the Emblem and includes the BS Fire Emblem story content as New Archanea Chronicles.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Nintendo DS/3DS hardware or a DS emulator with a legally dumped cartridge; no official English version exists.

entries.remaster_caveats: No official English release has shipped.

entries.title: Fire Emblem Awakening
entries.definitive_edition: Original 3DS release with DLC if already owned

emulation.notes: 3DS emulation can increase resolution, but DLC availability depends on legally owned content.

primary.version: Original 3DS release with DLC if already owned
primary.why: Awakening is a 3DS-exclusive entry; the most complete route is the original release with its downloadable maps already purchased before the 3DS eShop closure.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Nintendo 3DS hardware or 3DS emulation with legally dumped software; DLC completeness depends on prior ownership.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern port has shipped; DLC is not newly purchasable through the closed 3DS eShop.

entries.title: Fire Emblem Fates
entries.definitive_edition: Special Edition cartridge or owned all-path digital setup

emulation.notes: 3DS emulation can increase resolution, but only use legally owned game paths and DLC.

primary.version: Special Edition cartridge or owned digital all-path setup
primary.why: Fates is split across Birthright, Conquest, and Revelation; the best complete route is a setup that contains all three story paths, especially the Special Edition cartridge or already-purchased digital paths after the eShop closure.
primary.how_to_play: Use a Special Edition cartridge or a 3DS installation that already owns Birthright, Conquest, and Revelation.

entries.remaster_caveats: 3DS eShop closure makes newly completing the digital version difficult; physical Special Edition is the cleanest complete route.

entries.title: Fire Emblem Echoes: Shadows of Valentia
entries.definitive_edition: Original 3DS remake with DLC if already owned

emulation.notes: 3DS emulation can increase resolution, but DLC availability depends on legally owned content.

primary.version: Original 3DS remake with DLC if already owned
primary.why: Echoes is the 3DS remake of Gaiden and has no later port; the most complete route is the original 3DS release with owned DLC.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Nintendo 3DS hardware or 3DS emulation with legally dumped software; DLC completeness depends on prior ownership.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern port has shipped; DLC is not newly purchasable through the closed 3DS eShop.

entries.title: Fire Emblem: Three Houses
entries.definitive_edition: Switch release plus Expansion Pass / Cindered Shadows

emulation.notes: Use Nintendo Switch/Switch 2 hardware.

primary.version: Switch release plus Expansion Pass / Cindered Shadows
primary.why: Three Houses is a Switch-exclusive entry, and the Expansion Pass adds Cindered Shadows and other content, making it the most complete official route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Nintendo Switch or Switch 2 backward compatibility with the Expansion Pass installed.

entries.remaster_caveats: DLC ownership is required for Cindered Shadows and other Expansion Pass content.

entries.title: Fire Emblem Engage
entries.definitive_edition: Switch release plus Expansion Pass / Fell Xenologue

emulation.notes: Use Nintendo Switch/Switch 2 hardware.

primary.version: Switch release plus Expansion Pass / Fell Xenologue
primary.why: Engage is a Switch-exclusive entry, and the Expansion Pass adds the Fell Xenologue story plus additional characters and locations, making it the most complete official route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Nintendo Switch or Switch 2 backward compatibility with the Expansion Pass installed.

entries.remaster_caveats: DLC ownership is required for Fell Xenologue and other Expansion Pass content.

entries.title: BS Fire Emblem: Archanea Saga
entries.definitive_edition: New Archanea Chronicles in New Mystery of the Emblem

emulation.notes: Use New Mystery of the Emblem for the included episodes.

primary.version: New Archanea Chronicles in Fire Emblem: New Mystery of the Emblem
primary.why: The original Satellaview broadcasts are preservation-only today, while New Mystery of the Emblem includes the BS Fire Emblem story content as New Archanea Chronicles.
primary.how_to_play: Play the New Archanea Chronicles content inside Fire Emblem: New Mystery of the Emblem on Nintendo DS or DS emulation.

entries.remaster_caveats: No standalone official modern release exists.

entries.title: Tokyo Mirage Sessions #FE

emulation.notes: Use Nintendo Switch/Switch 2 hardware.

primary.why: Encore is the enhanced Switch version of the Wii U crossover and adds new songs, new outfits, a new storyline, and combat improvements.
primary.how_to_play: Play Tokyo Mirage Sessions #FE Encore on Nintendo Switch or Switch 2 backward compatibility.

entries.remaster_caveats: Encore is based on the international version and adds content; no separate Wii U-exclusive story content requires a secondary route.

entries.title: Fire Emblem Heroes

emulation.notes: Use a compatible smart device.

primary.why: Heroes is a mobile live-service crossover released for iOS and Android; the only meaningful route is the current app version.
primary.how_to_play: Install Fire Emblem Heroes on a compatible iOS or Android device and keep the app updated.

entries.remaster_caveats: Online service, account, region, and event availability affect content access.

entries.title: Fire Emblem Warriors
entries.definitive_edition: Nintendo Switch release plus Season Pass

emulation.notes: Use Nintendo Switch/Switch 2 hardware.

primary.why: The Switch version has higher fidelity than the New Nintendo 3DS version, and the Season Pass adds DLC packs that are not compatible with the New Nintendo 3DS version.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Nintendo Switch version with the Season Pass installed.

entries.remaster_caveats: Season Pass ownership is required for all DLC packs.

entries.title: Fire Emblem Warriors: Three Hopes

emulation.notes: Use Nintendo Switch/Switch 2 hardware.

primary.why: Three Hopes is a Switch-exclusive Warriors spinoff set in an alternate Three Houses timeline, with no separate DLC or enhanced edition required for the core route.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Nintendo Switch or Switch 2 backward compatibility.

entries.remaster_caveats: No enhanced edition has shipped.

entries.title: Fire Emblem Shadows

emulation.notes: Use a compatible smart device.

primary.why: Shadows is a smart-device Fire Emblem spinoff combining real-time strategy and social deduction; the only official route is the current iOS/Android app.
primary.how_to_play: Install Fire Emblem Shadows on a compatible iOS or Android device and keep the app updated.

entries.remaster_caveats: Online service, account, region, and event availability affect content access.
